Shred parsing and Merkle root computation with size and field validation.

# Purpose
This C file implements two functions for `fd_shred` records. The [`fd_shred_parse`](<#fd_shred_parse>) function validates a raw buffer as a shred and returns a typed `fd_shred_t` pointer only when the buffer size, shred type, header size, payload size, trailer size, and field values meet the expected rules. It checks both data shreds and code shreds, including legacy variants, and rejects invalid combinations such as bad type values, illegal offsets, invalid counters, and size mismatches.

The [`fd_shred_merkle_root`](<#fd_shred_merkle_root>) function computes the Merkle root for a shred and inserts the shred leaf into a Merkle tree with proof data. It derives the leaf position from shred fields, computes the protected byte range for the hash, and uses the shred's Merkle nodes to build the proof. Together, these functions provide parsing and Merkle verification support for shred data used by other code in the `fd_shred` interface.
